title: Spike: build-vs-adopt for chat UI library
description: Research spike (open question #9 in SPEC) to decide whether to adopt an existing React chat UI library or build custom components. Investigate candidates with permissive (MIT/Apache-2.0) licenses — `assistant-ui` is the named candidate; also evaluate `@chatscope/chat-ui-kit-react`, `stream-chat-react` (Stream Chat). License check follows `docs/15-engineering-conventions.md § 8`. Produce a written decision in the task notes covering: (1) license compatibility, (2) SSE/fetch-ReadableStream streaming support (must support POST + reader, not only EventSource), (3) FSD/barrel compatibility (no deep-import leakage, no global provider that hijacks routing), (4) bundle size impact, (5) Tailwind v4 token integration with `@aiflow/ui` theme. Recommendation defaults: if a library is MIT, supports custom fetch streaming, and renders message bubbles/avatar/empty/loading/error states via composable primitives we can drive from a hook → ADOPT it; otherwise BUILD custom components in `features/chat/ui/`. The decision becomes the input to the 'Create chat feature slice skeleton' task and all subsequent UI tasks — they reference the chosen primitive set. If no library is adopted, note the package list to install (or none) for the next task.
acceptance: A decision is recorded with the chosen approach (adopt `<lib>` version `<x>` OR build custom), the license name, the streaming mechanism it expects, and the exact list of UI tasks it implies. needsConfirmation is true so the user can approve before downstream UI tasks run.

title: Add tokensIn/tokensOut to ChatMessage schema template
description: Modify `packages/db/prisma/schema_project_template.prisma` ChatMessage model (lines 158-167) to add two nullable integer columns after `content`: `tokensIn Int?` and `tokensOut Int?`. Keep `createdAt`, `deletedAt`, and the `@@index([createdAt])` unchanged. Update the model comment block above ChatMessage to note these are best-effort token counts from the provider (nullable because a streaming mock and a dropped connection both leave them absent). Do NOT add a Prisma migration — project schemas are created from this template via `generateProjectSql` (packages/db/src/project-schema.ts), which runs `prisma migrate diff --from-empty`, so the new columns flow into the generated SQL automatically for any project created after this change. Then run `yarn prisma generate` (from `packages/db`) so the typed `ProjectClient` exposes `tokensIn`/`tokensOut` on `chatMessage`. Note: existing project schemas created before this change will NOT have the columns — per SPEC assumption #10, dev projects should be recreated (drop + recreate the project); prod migration is deferred. Call this out in the commit message.
acceptance: `schema_project_template.prisma` ChatMessage model has `tokensIn Int?` and `tokensOut Int?`. `yarn prisma generate` (in packages/db) succeeds and the regenerated `packages/db/generated/project` client types these fields on the model and on `chatMessage.create({ data })` / `chatMessage.findMany` selects. A newly created project (via the existing create-project flow) receives the columns — verify by inspecting the DDL output of `yarn tsx packages/db/scripts/generate-project-sql.ts project_test_x` or equivalent and confirming `"tokensIn"` / `"tokensOut"` appear in the CREATE TABLE for ChatMessage.

title: Fill ai-roles package: types and ModelProvider interface
description:
Create the type surface of `@aiflow/ai-roles` (currently `src/index.ts` is `export {};`). Files (2-3, each ≤ 200 lines):
1. `packages/ai-roles/src/types.ts` — exports interfaces exactly per SPEC § APIs and integrations:
   - `ChatRole = 'USER' | 'ASSISTANT' | 'SYSTEM'`
   - `interface ChatMessage { role: ChatRole; content: string }`
   - `interface ChatConfig { model: string; apiKey?: string; systemPrompt: string }`
   - `interface ModelProvider { chat(messages: ChatMessage[], config: ChatConfig): AsyncIterable<string> }`
   - `interface ChatResult { tokensIn: number | null; tokensOut: number | null }` — a side-channel for usage stats. To avoid changing the `chat()` AsyncIterable<string> signature, provide a separate method `chatWithUsage(messages, config): Promise<{ stream: AsyncIterable<string>; usage: Promise<ChatResult> }>` OR return an object whose `.stream` is the iterable and `.usage` resolves on completion. Pick the side-channel approach (object with `stream` + `usage` promise) since the route handler needs token counts after the stream closes.
2. `packages/ai-roles/src/index.ts` — barrel: `export * from './types'` plus the provider re-exports added by the next tasks. Keep `export *` scoped to types only for now.
Keep functions ≤ 50 lines, file ≤ 200 lines. No `@aiflow/` dependencies here — this package is a leaf.
acceptance: `packages/ai-roles/src/types.ts` exports the five named types above. `packages/ai-roles/src/index.ts` re-exports them. `yarn typecheck` (workspace root, which runs `tsc --noEmit` for ai-roles per its package.json script) passes. `ChatResult` (with nullable token counts) is exported — it is the type the route handler reads after the stream ends.

title: Implement ZaiProvider mock path (no API key)
description:
Create `packages/ai-roles/src/zai-provider.ts` implementing `ModelProvider` plus the side-channel usage contract. This task delivers the MOCK path only (when `process.env.ZAI_API_KEY` is absent) so local dev works without external network. The real HTTP path is a separate task. Requirements:
- `export class ZaiProvider implements ModelProvider`.
- `chat(messages, config)` returns `AsyncIterable<string>` — for the mock path, build a canned reply: if last user message present, echo back an interviewing analyst question (Russian, since the analyst prompt is Russian) prefixed with a fixed phrase, drawn from a small fixed array of 3-5 follow-up questions; split the canned reply into chunks by sentence/word and `yield` each after a `setTimeout`-style delay (use a helper `await delay(ms)` with ~30-80ms) so the consumer exercises real streaming.
- Implement the side-channel object form used by the route handler: `chatWithUsage(messages, config)` returns `{ stream: AsyncIterable<string>; usage: Promise<ChatResult> }` where the mock resolves `usage` to `{ tokensIn: null, tokensOut: null }` (per SPEC: mock may mark tokens null) once the stream is fully consumed.
- Export a factory `createZaiProvider()` that reads `ZAI_API_KEY` at construction; if absent, set an internal `mode='mock'`, else `mode='live'` (the live branch throws `not implemented` for now and is filled by the next task). Re-read the env per request is NOT required — one read per instance is fine.
Keep ≤ 200 lines. No `fetch` here yet.
dependencies: Fill ai-roles package: types and ModelProvider interface
acceptance: ZaiProvider class exists, instantiates in mock mode when ZAI_API_KEY is unset. Calling `for await (const chunk of provider.chat(messages, config))` yields 3+ string chunks with visible delay. The `usage` promise resolves to `{ tokensIn: null, tokensOut: null }`. Instantiating with a present-but-empty API key still falls back to mock. `yarn typecheck` passes.

title: Implement ZaiProvider live HTTP path (z.ai GLM streaming)
description:
Extend `packages/ai-roles/src/zai-provider.ts` with the live path (when `ZAI_API_KEY` is present). Make a real HTTPS streaming request to the z.ai API (GLM model) and return text chunks as an `AsyncIterable<string>`. Concrete steps:
- Use Node's built-in `fetch` (Node 22, available globally). POST to the z.ai chat completions endpoint with `stream: true`, `Authorization: Bearer ${ZAI_API_KEY}`, body `{ model: config.model, messages: [...systemPromptAsSystemMessage, ...messages], stream: true }`. The system prompt goes in as a single `{role:'SYSTEM', content: config.systemPrompt}` entry — translate internal `ChatRole` to the API's role names (USER/ASSISTANT map directly; SYSTEM→system).
- Parse the response body as an SSE stream of `data: {json}\n\n` lines. For each `choices[0].delta.content`, `yield` it. Stop on `data: [DONE]`.
- Capture the usage block if z.ai returns one in the final chunk (common shape: `{ usage: { prompt_tokens, completion_tokens } }`) and resolve the `usage` promise to `{ tokensIn: prompt_tokens ?? null, tokensOut: completion_tokens ?? null }`. If no usage arrives (provider-dependent), resolve to `{ tokensIn: null, tokensOut: null }` — never reject the usage promise.
- On non-2xx response or thrown reader error, throw an `Error` with a concise message — the route handler maps it to an SSE error frame.
If the exact z.ai endpoint/shape is uncertain, note the assumption in the task description and pick the OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions` shape (z.ai GLM exposes an OpenAI-compatible endpoint); set needsConfirmation if a guess is required. Keep ≤ 200 lines by extracting the SSE line-parser into a small helper function.
dependencies: Implement ZaiProvider mock path (no API key)
acceptance: With a valid `ZAI_API_KEY` set, `for await (const chunk of provider.chat(messages, config))` yields the model's streamed text. The `usage` promise resolves with token counts when the provider returns them, or with nulls otherwise. With `ZAI_API_KEY` unset, the mock path still runs (covered by the prior task). `yarn typecheck` passes.

title: Tests: ZaiProvider mock and live paths
description:
Add `packages/ai-roles/src/zai-provider.test.ts` (Vitest, runner already configured at `vitest.config.ts`). Cover:
1. Mock path (no ZAI_API_KEY): provider yields N>1 chunks, each a non-empty string; the `usage` promise resolves to `{ tokensIn: null, tokensOut: null }`; systemPrompt in config is accepted without error; messages with role USER/ASSISTANT/SYSTEM all accepted by the signature.
2. Live path with mocked `fetch`: stub `globalThis.fetch` (Vitest `vi.stubGlobal`) to return a `Response` whose `body` is a `ReadableStream` of encoded SSE lines: at minimum two content deltas and a final `data: [DONE]`, plus a usage chunk. Assert the provider yields the concatenated content in order and that `usage` resolves to the mocked `prompt_tokens`/`completion_tokens`. Assert a 4xx response causes `chat()` to throw.
3. Token extraction absence: stub `fetch` to a stream with NO usage block; assert `usage` resolves to nulls rather than rejecting.
Reset stubs with `afterEach(() => vi.unstubAllGlobals())`. Mock helper that builds the SSE response stream stays under 50 lines. Place the file beside `zai-provider.ts`. Run `yarn test packages/ai-roles`.
dependencies: Implement ZaiProvider live HTTP path (z.ai GLM streaming)
acceptance: `yarn test packages/ai-roles` passes with the three coverage areas above. Test for the live path does not hit the real network (fetch fully mocked). No test creates a real project schema.

title: Add chat feature slice: service layer (listMessages, saveMessage)
description:
Create the data-access half of the new `features/chat` slice following the FSD pattern of `features/projects/model/service.ts`. Files (≤ 200 lines each):
1. `apps/web/src/features/chat/model/types.ts` — `export interface ChatMessageView { id: string; role: 'USER'|'ASSISTANT'|'SYSTEM'; content: string; createdAt: Date }` and `export interface SaveMessageInput { role: 'USER'|'ASSISTANT'; content: string; tokensIn?: number|null; tokensOut?: number|null }`.
2. `apps/web/src/features/chat/model/service.ts` — functions taking a `ProjectClient` (from `@aiflow/db`) as a parameter so they are testable with a mock client, OR taking `schemaName` and calling `getProjectClient(schemaName)` internally like `projects` does. Prefer the `schemaName` form for consistency with projects/service.ts. Export:
   - `listMessages(schemaName: string): Promise<ChatMessageView[]>` — `getProjectClient(schemaName).chatMessage.findMany({ where: { deletedAt: null }, orderBy: { createdAt: 'asc' } })` and map to view (drop tokensIn/tokensOut from the view — they are not displayed).
   - `saveMessage(schemaName: string, input: SaveMessageInput): Promise<ChatMessageView>` — `create({ data: { role, content, tokensIn: input.tokensIn ?? null, tokensOut: input.tokensOut ?? null } })` and return the view.

3. `apps/web/src/features/chat/model/schema.ts` — helper `readSystemPrompt(): string` that resolves the path to `process.cwd() + '/.claude/agents/analyst.md'`, reads it synchronously (`readFileSync`), throws a clear error if missing. NOT cached (SPEC: read every request). Keep tiny.
Do NOT create `index.ts` yet — the barrel is added in a later task once the UI exists. This task is data + prompt-reading only.
dependencies: Add tokensIn/tokensOut to ChatMessage schema template
acceptance: `features/chat/model/{types,service,schema}.ts` exist. `listMessages` returns ascending-by-createdAt non-deleted messages. `saveMessage` persists with nullable tokens. `readSystemPrompt()` returns the contents of `.claude/agents/analyst.md`. `yarn typecheck` passes.

title: SSE chat API route: POST /api/projects/[id]/chat
description:
Create `apps/web/src/app/api/projects/[id]/chat/route.ts` exporting an async `POST` handler. Follow the auth+validation pattern of `app/api/projects/[id]/route.ts`. Sequence (per SPEC § APIs and integrations):
1. `const { id } = await params; const user = await requireUser();` then `if (!(await canAccessProject(user.id, id))) return 404` — do NOT leak project existence (matches `projects/[id]/route.ts` convention).
2. Parse JSON body `{ message: string }`; trim; if empty → 400 `{ error: 'Введите сообщение' }`.
3. Resolve the project's `schemaName`: load `ProjectMeta` via `getPublicClient().projectMeta.findUnique({ where: { id, deletedAt: null }, select: { schemaName: true, ownerId: true } })`; if missing or owner mismatch → 404 (defense-in-depth even though canAccessProject already covered it).
4. `saveMessage(schemaName, { role:'USER', content: trimmedMessage })` BEFORE streaming.
5. `const systemPrompt = readSystemPrompt()` (from `features/chat/model/schema`). `const history = await listMessages(schemaName)`.
6. Build `ChatConfig` from env: `{ model: process.env.ZAI_MODEL ?? 'glm-4.6', apiKey: process.env.ZAI_API_KEY, systemPrompt }`. `const provider = createZaiProvider(); const { stream, usage } = provider.chatWithUsage(history.map(toAdapterMessage), config)`.
7. Return `new Response(new ReadableStream({ async start(controller) {...} }), { headers: { 'Content-Type':'text/event-stream', 'Cache-Control':'no-cache, no-transform', 'Connection':'keep-alive' } })`. Inside `start`: `try { for await (const chunk of stream) controller.enqueue(encodeSse('data', JSON.stringify({ content: chunk }))); const u = await usage; await saveMessage(schemaName, { role:'ASSISTANT', content: <accumulated full text>, tokensIn: u.tokensIn, tokensOut: u.tokensOut }); controller.enqueue(encodeSse('data', '[DONE]')); } catch (e) { controller.enqueue(errorFrame(e)); } finally { controller.close(); } }`.
   - Accumulate chunks into a `fullText` string buffer so the ASSISTANT message is persisted as a single row of the complete answer (SPEC: full answer saved after stream; partial NOT saved on disconnect — a thrown error skips the save).
   - `encodeSse` helper: `event?` prefix + `data: ${payload}\n\n` encoded via `new TextEncoder().encode(...)`.
   - On error: emit `event: error\ndata: {"message":"..."}\n\n` then close. Do NOT rethrow into the client.
Keep the route ≤ 200 lines by extracting the SSE encoder and the body-validation into small helpers in the same file. Russian user-facing error strings.
dependencies: Add chat feature slice: service layer (listMessages, saveMessage)
Implement ZaiProvider live HTTP path (z.ai GLM streaming)
acceptance: POST to `/api/projects/<existing-id>/chat` with `{ message: 'hi' }` as an authenticated owner returns `Content-Type: text/event-stream` and yields `data: {"content":...}` frames followed by `data: [DONE]`. POST with empty message → 400. POST as non-owner / unknown id → 404. After a successful request, two new ChatMessage rows exist (USER + ASSISTANT) with the assistant row's tokensIn/tokensOut populated when the provider returned them. A thrown provider error emits an `event: error` frame and does NOT persist an ASSISTANT row.

title: Tests: SSE chat route handler
description:
Add `apps/web/src/app/api/projects/[id]/chat/route.test.ts` (Vitest). Mock the dependencies: `vi.mock('@/features/auth')` to return a fixed user and make `canAccessProject` return true/false per test; `vi.mock('@/features/chat/model/service')` to capture saveMessage calls and return canned listMessages; `vi.mock('@aiflow/ai-roles')` to return a fake provider whose `chatWithUsage` returns `{ stream: asyncIterableOf(['Hello',' ', 'world']), usage: Promise.resolve({ tokensIn: 5, tokensOut: 3 }) }`. Cover:
1. Happy path: invoke the exported `POST` with a Request carrying `{ message: 'hi' }`; read the returned Response body reader; assert the decoded frames are `data: {"content":"Hello"}`, `data: {"content":" "}`, `data: {"content":"world"}`, then `data: [DONE]`; assert `saveMessage` was called twice (USER then ASSISTANT with `tokensIn:5, tokensOut:3` and accumulated content `'Hello world'`).
2. Empty message → 400, no saveMessage calls, no stream.
3. Forbidden (canAccessProject false) → 404, no provider call.
4. Provider throws → assert an `event: error` frame is emitted, the stream closes, and the ASSISTANT saveMessage is NOT called (USER saveMessage WAS called, since it precedes streaming).
Keep the test file under 200 lines by sharing a `makeRequest(body)` helper.
acceptance: `yarn test apps/web/src/app/api/projects/[id]/chat` passes with all four cases. No real HTTP server or DB is started.

title: Chat UI: message list, input, send hook (client component)
description:
Build the chat interaction UI inside the `features/chat/ui` slice, following the decision from the spike task (adopt `<lib>` OR build custom). If building custom, create:
1. `apps/web/src/features/chat/ui/ChatPanel.tsx` ('use client', ≤ 200 lines) — receives `initialMessages: ChatMessageView[]` and `projectId: string`. Renders: a scrollable message list (each message: avatar circle labelled AI for ASSISTANT / 'Я' for USER, bubble with `content` and a formatted `createdAt` time), an empty state ('Опишите идею вашего приложения'), a streaming state indicator ('Аналитик печатает…') shown while awaiting/reading the stream, an error state ('Что-то пошло не так, попробуйте ещё раз'). Auto-scroll to bottom on new chunks (a `useRef` + `scrollIntoView`). Visual differentiation: user bubbles right-aligned with accent border, analyst bubbles left-aligned neutral — using `@aiflow/ui` tokens (`bg-surface`, `border-primary`, `text-fg`).
2. `apps/web/src/features/chat/ui/ChatInput.tsx` ('use client', ≤ 100 lines) — multiline `<textarea>` (NOT `<Input>` since Input is single-line; reuse the cn styling), 'Отправить' Button from `@aiflow/ui`. Enter to send (Shift+Enter for newline). Disabled while streaming.
3. `apps/web/src/features/chat/model/useChat.ts` ('use client', ≤ 150 lines) — hook returning `{ messages, streaming, error, send }`. `send(text)` performs `fetch('/api/projects/'+projectId+'/chat', { method:'POST', body: JSON.stringify({message:text}), headers:{'Content-Type':'application/json'} })`, reads `response.body.getReader()`, decodes via `TextDecoder`, splits on `\n\n`, parses `data:` lines, and on `data: [DONE]` finalises. On `event: error` sets the error state. Accumulates `content` chunks into the in-progress assistant message. Does NOT optimistically insert the user message twice — append the user message once at send time, then append the assistant message that grows as chunks arrive.
If ADOPTING a library, replace steps 1-3 with the library's composable primitives wired to the same `useChat`-equivalent data flow; keep the same public component API (`<ChatPanel initialMessages projectId />`) so the page task is unaffected. Use Tailwind classes consistent with the rest of the app; Russian for user-facing strings.
dependencies: Spike: build-vs-adopt for chat UI library
acceptance: `<ChatPanel>` renders an empty-state message when `initialMessages=[]`. The `useChat` hook successfully streams from the route (manual check via a temporary page is acceptable; the real page is wired in the next task). Enter sends, Shift+Enter inserts a newline. While streaming, the input is disabled and 'Аналитик печатает…' shows. On error, the error message shows. Files all ≤ 200 lines, `yarn typecheck` and `yarn lint` pass.

title: Researcher page: left artifacts panel + chat panel layout
description:
Create the server-rendered page `apps/web/src/app/(app)/projects/[id]/research/page.tsx` (URL: `/projects/[id]/research`) following the pattern of `app/(app)/projects/[id]/page.tsx`. Steps:
1. `export default async function ResearcherPage({ params }: { params: Promise<{ id: string }> })`. `const { id } = await params; const user = await requireUser();` then resolve the project: `const project = await getProject(id, user.id)` (reuse from `@/features/projects`); `if (!project) notFound();`.
2. Resolve `schemaName` for the project (query `projectMeta` for `schemaName` — add a tiny helper or reuse a select in `getProject`; if `getProject` does not expose `schemaName`, fetch it here via `getPublicClient().projectMeta.findUnique({ where:{id}, select:{schemaName:true} })`). Load `const messages = await listMessages(schemaName)`.
3. Render a two-column responsive layout: left ~20% artifacts panel, right ~80% `<ChatPanel initialMessages={messages} projectId={id} />`. Below 768px the left panel collapses (`hidden md:block`) and chat is full-width.
4. Left panel content (all static/placeholder per MVP-0): a Card titled 'Спецификация' showing 'Спецификация не создана'; a 'Загруженные файлы' list showing 'Нет файлов'; a Link 'Дорожная карта' → `/projects/[id]/tasks`; a Button 'Создать спецификацию' that on click does nothing OR shows a toast 'Генерация спецификации будет доступна позже' (use a tiny client component or inline onClick). Mark the button with `aria-disabled`/tooltip so it is visibly inert. Use `@aiflow/ui` primitives (Card, Button, Input-equivalents) and Tailwind tokens. Russian strings throughout. Keep ≤ 200 lines.
acceptance: Navigating to `/projects/<id>/research` as the project owner renders the two-panel layout, the chat panel shows existing history (or the empty-state prompt), and the artifacts panel shows the three placeholder items. Navigating as a non-owner or to an unknown id returns 404 (via `notFound()`). The 'Создать спецификацию' button is visibly inert. The page is responsive below 768px (left panel hidden).

title: Smoke test: chat round-trip end-to-end
description:
Final verification task exercising the primary user path: load the Researcher page → send a message → receive a streamed response → verify persistence. Run as a manual/ scripted check documented in the task description (no new code unless a tiny Playwright/Vitest integration test already has scaffolding — check `vitest.config.ts` covers only unit tests, so this is a written manual run with explicit steps and expected outputs, NOT an automated e2e suite). Steps to perform and report:
1. With `ZAI_API_KEY` UNSET (mock mode): start the dev DB if needed, ensure a fresh project exists (or recreate one so the new ChatMessage columns are present), sign in, open `/projects/<id>/research`, confirm the empty state.
2. Type 'Хочу приложение для заметок' and send. Verify: 'Аналитик печатает…' shows, text streams in chunk by chunk, the input disables during streaming, then re-enables when done; the assistant message remains visible.
3. Reload the page. Verify: both the user message AND the full assistant message persist and render in order (tokens not shown, but persistence proves saveMessage ran).
4. (If a `ZAI_API_KEY` is available) repeat with the live provider; otherwise document that the live path was covered by the unit test with mocked fetch.
5. Trigger an error path: temporarily break the provider (e.g. set an invalid `ZAI_MODEL` or stop the dev server mid-stream) and confirm the error frame shows, the assistant row is NOT persisted, and the user row IS.
Report each step's pass/fail with observed output. If any step fails, file the failure as a follow-up rather than marking this task done.
dependencies: Researcher page: left artifacts panel + chat panel layout
Tests: ZaiProvider mock and live paths
acceptance: All five steps pass (step 4 may be skipped if no key is available, with a note). The mock-mode round-trip (steps 1-3) and the error path (step 5) MUST pass. Persistence verified by reload. The task is reported as a written checklist of pass/fail results, not as new test code.
